name: Acquired Factor V Deficiency

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Acquired Factor V Deficiency Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Prolonged prothrombin time (PT) and activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) not corrected by mixing studies
Markedly reduced factor V activity levels in plasma
Detection of factor V inhibitors by Bethesda assay or similar inhibitor assays
Clinical evidence of bleeding disproportionate to other coagulation abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of prolonged PT and aPTT not corrected by mixing studies, low factor V activity, and detection of factor V inhibitor
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of congenital factor V deficiency and other coagulopathies.

pathognomonic.notes: Includes epistaxis, gum bleeding, and menorrhagia
searchTerms: severe bleeding from skin and mucous membranes
heavy bleeding in mouth and skin
bleeding lasts long after small cuts

occasional.symptomName: Anemia secondary to chronic blood loss
searchTerms: low red blood cells from ongoing blood loss

rare.notes: May be associated with underlying autoimmune conditions

laboratory: Prolonged PT and aPTT not corrected by mixing studies
Presence of factor V inhibitors detected by Bethesda assay
Normal levels of other coagulation factors
imaging: Imaging to identify bleeding sites such as CT for intracranial hemorrhage or ultrasound for retroperitoneal bleeding
genetic: No genetic mutations as this is an acquired disorder
other: History of exposure to bovine thrombin or other triggers such as antibiotics, autoimmune diseases, or malignancies

redFlags: Sudden onset of severe bleeding without prior bleeding history
Failure of bleeding to improve with standard plasma transfusions
Prolonged coagulation times not corrected by mixing studies
references: Franchini M, Lippi G. Acquired factor V inhibitors: a systematic review. J Thromb Thrombolysis. 2011;31(3):449-457.
Orphanet: Acquired factor V deficiency - ORPHA:599490
Nishimura J, et al. Clinical features and treatment of acquired factor V inhibitors. Blood Coagul Fibrinolysis. 2018;29(2):171-176.
